methodology.Volume: Sum of tokens paid into maker wallets during Aqua swap execution, measured as Pushed events on the Aqua registries (the current AquaRouter and the original developer-release registry). Only the taker-paid side of each swap is counted, to avoid double counting and to include the maker fee (the Pulled side is net of fees and would undercount). Pushed events emitted by strategy deployment (the consecutive run following a Shipped event for the same strategy) only register virtual balances without moving tokens and are excluded. When a maker's own strategies trade against each other within one transaction, the tokens the maker receives are netted against what it pays out of the same token, so only the net change counts.

Recurring subscription payments settled to recipients, summed on-chain from SubscriptionProcessed events of the AxiumPass SubscriptionVault contracts (v1 and v2) on each chain. Only the stablecoins AxiumPass offers at checkout are counted (USDC, USDT, EURC — per-chain allowlist in the adapter): the v1 vault is permissionless on the token argument, so any other ERC-20 that reached it is excluded rather than reported as subscription volume, which keeps the reported figure denominated in the tokens named here. Each counted amount is pulled from the subscriber and forwarded 100% to the recipient in the same transaction. The vaults are non-custodial and charge no on-chain fee, so no fees/revenue is reported. Limitation: the v1 vault is also permissionless on enrolment, so a subscription created from an address to itself is indistinguishable on-chain from a merchant payment and is counted; excluding it would require filtering on AxiumPass's enrolled-recipient set, which is not present in the logs.

methodology.Revenue: What reaches the protocol, counted when the fee is taken: the protocol fee each Swap event carries; the protocol's share of a launch pool's liquidity fees under the pool's permanent LP lock split, only where the locks provably hold all of the pool's liquidity; and the protocol's share of the creator tax and guard trade fee under the split the guard stores for that pool. A split that cannot be read is never guessed: that amount is left out of Revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All of Revenue. Latch has no token, so nothing is diverted to holders.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Fees minus Revenue: swap fees earned by liquidity providers, and the shares of locked-liquidity fees, creator tax and guard trade fees that go to launch creators and integrators (and any guard-taken amount whose split could not be read).
methodology.Volume: Gross input of every swap on CLPoolManager and BinPoolManager, one leg per swap. Swaps in Latch's own test tokens (LTT1/LTT2 on Robinhood Chain) are excluded: they have no market and no price.

Fees.Launch Trade Fees: The part of a launch pool's trade fee that the launch guard takes itself (FeeTaken).
Fees.Creator Tax: Buy/sell tax a launch pool's guard takes after the swap (TaxTaken).

UserFees.Token Swap Fees: Swap fee charged by the pool, read from each Swap event.
UserFees.Launch Trade Fees: The part of a launch pool's trade fee that the launch guard takes itself (FeeTaken).
UserFees.Creator Tax: Buy/sell tax a launch pool's guard takes after the swap (TaxTaken).

Revenue.Swap Fees To Protocol: Protocol fee slice of the swap fee, at the rate each Swap event carried on chain.
Revenue.Locked Liquidity Fees To Protocol: Protocol share of a launch pool's liquidity fees under its LP lock split.
Revenue.Launch Trade Fees To Protocol: Protocol share of the guard-taken trade fee under the pool's fee split.
Revenue.Creator Tax To Protocol: Protocol share of the creator tax under the pool's tax split.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees To Protocol: Protocol fee slice of the swap fee, at the rate each Swap event carried on chain.
ProtocolRevenue.Locked Liquidity Fees To Protocol: Protocol share of a launch pool's liquidity fees under its LP lock split.
ProtocolRevenue.Launch Trade Fees To Protocol: Protocol share of the guard-taken trade fee under the pool's fee split.
ProtocolRevenue.Creator Tax To Protocol: Protocol share of the creator tax under the pool's tax split.

SupplySideRevenue.Swap Fees To Liquidity Providers: Swap fee remaining after the protocol slice, earned by liquidity providers.
SupplySideRevenue.Locked Liquidity Fees To Creators And In: Creator and integrator shares of a launch pool's liquidity fees under its LP lock split.
SupplySideRevenue.Launch Trade Fees To Creators And Integr: Creator and integrator shares of the guard-taken trade fee.
SupplySideRevenue.Launch Trade Fees, Split Not Read: Guard-taken trade fee whose split could not be read; none of it is counted as Revenue.
SupplySideRevenue.Creator Tax To Creators And Integrators: Creator and integrator shares of the creator tax.
SupplySideRevenue.Creator Tax, Split Not Read: Creator tax whose split could not be read; none of it is counted as Revenue.

methodology.Volume: Native coin paid on buys and received on sells on ADEXTO bonding curves, gross of fees. Trades by the ADEXTO team's own wallets are excluded.
methodology.Fees: All swap fees paid by traders on ADEXTO bonding curves, read from each Swap event: the creator, curve reserve, buyback and protocol legs. Rates are set per market at launch and never change; the launch presets are 1.00% on factory 1.0.0 and 0.12.0 markets and 0.40% on factory 0.11.0 markets.
methodology.UserFees: All swap fees paid by traders.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol leg of every swap, paid to the ADEXTO protocol treasury: 0.10% of the trade on factory 0.11.0, 0.12.0 and 1.0.0 markets, where it is a factory constant. Factory 0.10.0 markets have no protocol leg.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol leg of every swap, paid to the ADEXTO protocol treasury: 0.10% of the trade on factory 0.11.0, 0.12.0 and 1.0.0 markets, where it is a factory constant. Factory 0.10.0 markets have no protocol leg.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator leg paid to each market's creator, the reserve leg that stays in the market's curve, and the buyback leg that buys and burns the market's own token.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: Swap fees paid on ADEXTO bonding curves, read from the fee legs every Swap event carries.

UserFees.Token Swap Fees: Swap fees paid by traders on ADEXTO bonding curves.

Revenue.Swap Fees To Protocol: The protocol leg, accrued on each curve and claimable only to the immutable ADEXTO protocol treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees To Protocol: The protocol leg, accrued on each curve and claimable only to the immutable ADEXTO protocol treasury.

SupplySideRevenue.Swap Fees To Creators: The creator leg, claimable only to the market's immutable creator. Launch presets: 0.70% of each trade on factory 1.0.0 and 0.12.0 markets, 0.10% on factory 0.11.0 markets; actual amounts are read from each Swap event.
SupplySideRevenue.Swap Fees To Curve Reserves: The depth leg, which stays in the market's curve reserve and raises its price floor.
SupplySideRevenue.Swap Fees To Token Buyback And Burn: The buyback leg, spent only on buying and burning the market's own token.

methodology.Volume: Stablecoin amount of every completed P2P trade, read from the VailoxEscrow EscrowComplete events. Each trade is counted once (the off-chain fiat leg is not added) and cancelled or refunded trades are excluded.
methodology.Fees: Escrow fees paid by sellers and buyers on completed P2P trades, read from EscrowComplete events. Fees are tiered by trade size (fixed fee below 50 USD, then 1.25% down to 0.25%) with a lower rate for verified merchants. Cancelled or refunded trades pay no fee.
methodology.UserFees: All escrow fees are paid directly by the trading users.
methodology.Revenue: All escrow fees are kept by the protocol.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All escrow fees go to the protocol treasury.

Fees.Seller Escrow Fees: Fee paid by the seller on top of the escrowed amount, charged when the trade completes.
Fees.Buyer Escrow Fees: Fee deducted from the amount the buyer receives when the trade completes.

UserFees.Seller Escrow Fees: Fee paid by the seller on top of the escrowed amount, charged when the trade completes.
UserFees.Buyer Escrow Fees: Fee deducted from the amount the buyer receives when the trade completes.

Revenue.Seller Escrow Fees To Protocol: Seller escrow fees credited to the protocol on completion.
Revenue.Buyer Escrow Fees To Protocol: Buyer escrow fees credited to the protocol on completion.

ProtocolRevenue.Seller Escrow Fees To Protocol: Seller escrow fees credited to the protocol on completion.
ProtocolRevenue.Buyer Escrow Fees To Protocol: Buyer escrow fees credited to the protocol on completion.

methodology.Fees: Swap fees charged by DeepCore pools, read from each Swap event (protocol fee included), plus the fee DeepCore's router charges on fills it routes to other venues, read from its Filled events. Launch-pool creator taxes and launch-guard trade fees are not counted.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol fee slice each Swap event carried, plus the router fee on routed fills. Both are paid to the protocol.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol fee slice each Swap event carried, plus the router fee on routed fills. Both are paid to the protocol.

methodology.Volume: USDC players spend opening Raflux gacha packs of physical trading cards (Super Gacha on Solana, FluxBox on Base), at the full pack price including any part covered by a coupon. Packs are sold at fixed prices of 10, 25, 50 and 100 USDC (1 USDC packs on Base at launch); each pack pulls a physical card, often with a USDC bonus, that the player can ship home or sell back for USDC.
methodology.Fees: Pack purchases minus USDC returned to players: refunds of cancelled pulls, card cash-outs, sell-backs, USDC prizes and reimbursed card shipments. This is the 10% fee Raflux keeps when a card is exchanged for USDC plus the game result of pulls, so it is negative on days when players win more than they pay.
methodology.Revenue: Pack purchases minus USDC returned to players, kept by Raflux. No share goes to LPs, referrers or token holders.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Pack purchases minus USDC returned to players, all of it sent to the Raflux treasury.

Fees.Pack Purchases: USDC players spend opening packs, at the full pack price including any part covered by a coupon.
Fees.Buybacks: USDC returned to players: refunds of cancelled pulls, card cash-outs, sell-backs, USDC prizes and reimbursed card shipments.

Revenue.Pack Purchases: USDC players spend opening packs, kept by Raflux before player payouts.
Revenue.Buybacks: USDC returned to players, subtracted from revenue kept by Raflux.

ProtocolRevenue.Pack Purchases: USDC players spend opening packs, sent to the Raflux treasury before player payouts.
ProtocolRevenue.Buybacks: USDC returned to players, subtracted from treasury revenue.

SupplySideRevenue.Card Procurement, Grading & Vaulting: The platform buys the physical cards behind its packs and pays to grade, ship and vault them. These costs are paid offchain and not disclosed.

methodology.Volume: Service payments in USDC on Base settled through Central City's immutable fee routers with the fee included: the full price the router moves for each payment (90% to the seller, 10% fee to the treasury). Fee-on-top payments, where the router moves only the fee, are not counted. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.
methodology.Fees: The 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments, which AI agents make in USDC on Base for services on Central City's Feed (other payments carry no fee), charged by Central City's immutable fee routers and sent straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.
methodology.Revenue: The full 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments, which AI agents make in USDC on Base for services on Central City's Feed, kept by Central City: the immutable fee routers send it straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The full 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments, which AI agents make in USDC on Base for services on Central City's Feed, sent by Central City's immutable fee routers straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.

Fees.Service Fees: The 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments in USDC on Base, charged by Central City's immutable fee routers and sent straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.

Revenue.Service Fees To Treasury: The full 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments in USDC on Base, sent by Central City's immutable fee routers straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.

ProtocolRevenue.Service Fees To Treasury: The full 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments in USDC on Base, sent by Central City's immutable fee routers straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.

methodology.Volume: Gross USDC players pay to open card packs, including draws that are later refunded.
methodology.Fees: USDC players pay to open card packs, net of refunds and instant buybacks of won cards, plus marketplace fees on card trades.
methodology.Revenue: Pack sales net of refunds and buybacks, minus payouts to third-party card stakers, referral commissions and draw fees sent to the Jackpot, plus marketplace fees. Payouts for cards staked by the platform's own wallets stay in revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Pack sales net of refunds and buybacks, minus payouts to third-party card stakers, referral commissions and draw fees sent to the Jackpot, plus marketplace fees, all kept by the TopMarket treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Card prices and profit shares paid or credited to third-party stakers whose cards were won, referral commissions settled to referrers, and draw fees routed to the Jackpot prize pool since October 2026.

Fees.Gacha Pack Sales: USDC paid for pack draws including the draw fee, minus refunded draws.
Fees.Card Buybacks: Instant buybacks paid to winners who sell their card back instead of keeping it; subtracted.
Fees.Marketplace Fees: Platform fee the Marketplace sends to its fee recipient on each card sale, accepted offer and settled auction.

SupplySideRevenue.Card Payouts To Stakers: Card price (keep) or profit share (recycle) paid or credited to third-party stakers at settlement; later withdrawals of existing credits and payouts to the platform Safe and treasury are excluded.
SupplySideRevenue.Jackpot Contributions: Draw fees routed to the Jackpot prize pool, which pays them back to players.
SupplySideRevenue.Referral Commissions: Referral commissions TopMarket settles to referrers off-chain, taken from its public settlement feed when they settle.

Revenue.Gacha Pack Sales To Protocol: Pack sales net of refunds, minus payouts to third-party card stakers, pack referral commissions and Jackpot contributions.
Revenue.Card Buybacks: Instant buybacks paid to winners who sell their card back; subtracted.
Revenue.Marketplace Fees To Protocol: Marketplace fees received by the treasury, minus marketplace referral commissions.

ProtocolRevenue.Gacha Pack Sales To Protocol: Pack sales net of refunds, minus payouts to third-party card stakers, pack referral commissions and Jackpot contributions.
ProtocolRevenue.Card Buybacks: Instant buybacks paid to winners who sell their card back; subtracted.
ProtocolRevenue.Marketplace Fees To Protocol: Marketplace fees received by the treasury, minus marketplace referral commissions.

SupplySideRevenue.Card Procurement, Grading & Vaulting: The platform buys the physical cards behind its packs and pays to grade, ship and vault them. These costs are paid offchain and not disclosed.

methodology.Volume: Gross quote-asset value of every buy and sell on CURB bonding curves (CurveBuy quoteIn; CurveSell quoteOut + fee + tax). Trading in graduated Uniswap v4 pools is excluded: it is counted by the Uniswap v4 adapter.
methodology.Fees: The trading tax (1%-5%, set per launch) paid on every curve and graduated-pool trade, in the quote asset. The pools' 0.05% Uniswap v4 LP fee is not included: it is earned by the pool's liquidity and already counted by the Uniswap v4 adapter.
methodology.UserFees: Traders pay the whole trading tax. Launching costs gas only.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's share of the tax (0.50% of the trade at deployment, frozen into each launch), plus the creator share of launches whose creator wallet is the treasury ($CURB).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The platform's share of the tax on both venues, plus the creator share of treasury-created launches ($CURB), paid to the treasury Safe.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the tax: to the launch's creator, or to the launch's own token holders through its distributor once holder sharing is on.

Fees.Bonding Curve Trading Tax: Platform share (fee) plus creator share (tax) of every CurveBuy and CurveSell on the bonding curve of a launch created by a CURB factory.
Fees.Graduated Pool Trading Tax: Every leg of the tax the FeeHook takes from a graduated pool swap, paid out (FeePaidDirect) or recorded as owed (FeeAccrued).

UserFees.Bonding Curve Trading Tax: Trading tax paid by bonding-curve traders.
UserFees.Graduated Pool Trading Tax: Trading tax paid by graduated-pool traders.

Revenue.Trading Tax To Treasury: The platform's share of the tax on both venues, plus the creator share of treasury-created launches ($CURB), paid to the treasury Safe.

ProtocolRevenue.Trading Tax To Treasury: The platform's share of the tax on both venues, plus the creator share of treasury-created launches ($CURB), paid to the treasury Safe.

SupplySideRevenue.Creator Fees: Creator share of the tax, paid to the launch's creator wallet.
SupplySideRevenue.Trading Tax To Launch Holders: Creator share of the tax on launches with holder sharing on, paid to the launch's distributor and split among that launch's token holders.
